To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

interleukin‐ 1 receptor antagonist (a naturally occurring inhibitor of interleukin 1) exhibits significant neuroprotectective effects in an in vitro model of brain injury when applied within 16 hr after the onset of the insult, and that interleukin 2 receptor antagonist (a natural occurring inhibitor of interleuikin 1) also exhibits neuroprotective effects when applied 16 hr after injury, although to a lesser extent than when applied within 8 hr after the onset.
interleukin‐ (IL‐) 1β is a mediator of excitotoxic neuronal cell death and microglial and astrocyte activation in rat organotypically cultured hippocampal slices.

interleukin‐(IL‐1) receptor antagonist (IL1‐RA) exhibits significant neuroprotecting effects in a rat organotypic culture of hippocampal slices (OHSC) when administered within the first 24 hours after excitotoxic neuronal damage.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of IL‐1 in the pathogenesis of excitotoxic injury and with its possible application for therapeutic interventions.
the development and application of novel methods for the detection and quantification of microglia.
the question whether the interleukin‐ (IL)‐6 system can be involved in the pathogenesis of multiple sclerosis (MS) and whether it can serve as an additional therapeutic target in this disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
IL‐1RA can be administered with a certain time delay after injury and is still effective in suppressing neuronal damage, microglial activation, and IL‐β production in OHSC.
IL‐1RA has a neuroprotective effect, but that this effect is time‐limited, and the effect on microglial activation seems to be delayed and weaker.
IL‐1RA has significant neuroprotective potential in the treatment of excitotoxic brain injury, even if applied after the onset of the injury.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the IL‐1 receptor is a potential drug target for the treatment of stroke.
we have demonstrated that IL‐1RA is a potent neuroprotectant in an in vitro model of NMDA excitotoxicity.
the neurotoxicity of IL‐1 is a late event and can be inhibited by IL‐1RA even when applied 36 hr after injury.
The main takeaway from our work is that
IL‐1RA is effective in reducing neuronal damage and microgliosis even when applied 16 hours after injury.
IL‐1RA can be applied with a certain time window after injury and is effective in reducing neuronal damage and microgliosis.

IL‐1 receptor antagonism is a viable therapeutic approach for the prevention and treatment of acute central nervous system injury and that the time window of therapeutic efficacy is much wider than previously thought.
